stories.headline: Rasmus Højlund on aiming Man United dig at Man City fans: 'Some good banter'
stories.summary: Former United striker Rasmus Hojlund confirmed he shouted "there's only one team in Manchester" towards the City fans after scoring for Napoli.
stories.body:
Former Manchester United striker Rasmus Højlund confirmed he shouted "there's only one team in Manchester" towards the Manchester City fans after scoring for Napoli in their Champions League clash at the Etihad on Tuesday.

Højlund, who scored 14 goals in 62 matches across his three years at Old Trafford, scored the opener in the 2-2 league phase draw.

Asked whether he could confirm he had said the comment, Højlund told TNT Sports: "Yeah, indeed. Yeah, just some good banter. There's the rivalry between Manchester City and Man United, and obviously I have a past in Manchester United, so that's my club. Nothing against Man City, but yeah, United is my club."

Højlund joined Napoli on a season-long loan deal ahead of last season. The switch was made permanent when the club qualified for the Champions League with their second-place finish in Serie A.

He continued: "It's good to score here, good point. And yeah, happy for that."

Ayyoub Bouaddi got City level with his first goal for the club in the second half before Noa Lang put the Italian side back in front. Rayan Cherki rescued a point for the hosts with a solo effort four minutes from time.

The result leaves Enzo Maresca's out-of-form side with just one win from their last seven matches in all competitions.

- Cherki unhappy despite salvaging Man City draw: 'Don't care about my goal'

Tuesday's encounter marked the return of City legend Kevin De Bruyne to the Etihad after he left for Napoli last year.

De Bruyne, along with Scott McTominay -- another former Man United midfielder -- and Billy Gilmour, was instrumental in helping earn Napoli a point that boosts their hopes of qualifying for the knockout rounds.

"I think the other two gets a lot of praise. Scott and Kevin, incredible players, one of them with an amazing history and Scott doing absolutely fantastic now," Højlund said. "But yeah, sometimes we forget Gilmore and he's done really well this season. He's got more minutes than he did last year."

City, who sit sixth in the league phase table, travel to face Barcelona in their next Champions League outing on Dec. 8 while Napoli host Club Brugge.

stories.headline: Broncos' Sean Payton: J.K. Dobbins suspended one game for detrimental conduct
stories.summary: The Broncos suspended running back J.K. Dobbins for one game for conduct detrimental to the team.
stories.body:
ENGLEWOOD, Colo. -- Denver Broncos coach Sean Payton said Tuesday he has suspended running back J.K. Dobbins for Friday's game against the Pittsburgh Steelers due to "conduct detrimental.''

Dobbins will not practice or take part in any team activities this week. The Broncos (8-2) face the Steelers on Friday at Acrisure Stadium in Pittsburgh.

"There is one team announcement, I'm not going to comment afterwards, I'm suspending J.K. Dobbins for this weekend's game, conduct detrimental, that's all I'm going to say about it,'' Payton said after Tuesday's practice. "Head coach's decision.''

Asked if he wanted to elaborate on any of the circumstances that surrounded the decision, Payton said no and added "think it's better that way.''

Dobbins was in the Broncos' facility earlier on Tuesday and then left, multiple team sources said. Payton then told players of the suspension in the team's normally-scheduled group meeting.

Dobbins, in his second season with the team and a player Payton had called one of the "top priorities'' to re-sign this past offseason, had one carry, for no gain, in the Broncos' 38-24 victory Sunday over the Las Vegas Raiders. It marked the first time since the 2020 season Dobbins had a single carry in a game he was in uniform to play -- he had two one-carry games for the Baltimore Ravens that year.

Dobbins was visibly frustrated at times on the sideline during Sunday's game and high-fiving teammates at other times. When asked about the running back rotation Monday, Payton had offered that Dobbins "is healthy'' and that "J.K. is going to be super important for what we're doing in this stretch.''

Jonah Coleman, who sat out four games earlier this season because of an ankle injury, has steadily received more work since his Week 7 return to the lineup. Coleman got 24 of the team's 27 carries by running backs in Sunday's win. Coleman's 111 yards rushing were also the team's first 100-yard rushing game since Dobbins' 111 yards rushing in a Week 8 win last season over the Dallas Cowboys.

The Broncos also designated running back Tyler Badie for return from injured reserve Tuesday and Badie practiced with the team and was listed as a full participant. Asked if Badie would play Friday or how the rotation might look against the Steelers, Payton said, "I'm not going to get into who's playing.''

Running back RJ Harvey (knee) is eligible to return from injured reserve next week.

Quarterback Bo Nix, when asked about the suspension, said: "Well, obviously I have nothing to do with it,'' Nix said. "Just keep finding our way to figure out how to win games, fortunately it has nothing to do with me.''

Cornerback Pat Surtain II, also a team captain like Nix, offered a similar answer with, "I ain't got nothing much to say, it's coach's decision at the end of the day.''

It's all a long way from Dobbins' promise -- he termed it a "pinkie swear'' -- both during the team's minicamp in June as well as training camp, that he would play in every game this season and lead the league in rushing.

"This year, forget a top-three, I keep saying it, people think I'm crazy but I'm going to be No. 1, and I'm going to keep it there for the whole year,'' Dobbins said in August. "You know, 17 games. A lot of people get mad when I say the injuries are over, cause I said it last year, but that one was pretty fluky, right? This year there won't be any.''

Dobbins has dealt with several injuries in his career, including a career-threatening knee injury, and he sat out the final seven regular-season games because of a foot injury as well as both of the Broncos' playoff games last season. His 15 games played in 2020, as a rookie for the Baltimore Ravens, is still the most games he has played in a season.

It is believed Dobbins, who signed a two-year, $16 million deal with the team this past offseason, is the first player suspended by the Broncos during a season for conduct detrimental to the team since wide receiver Brandon Marshall in 2009.

stories.headline: Tyrese, Jade Haliburton announce they are expecting their first child
stories.summary: The couple wed in August after seven years of dating and announced the news that they're expecting on Instagram.
stories.body:
Indiana Pacers star Tyrese Haliburton and his wife, Jade, are expecting their first child, the couple announced Tuesday in a joint post on Instagram.

They shared the news with a photoshoot that featured their apricot labradoodle, Ames, wearing an apron that said "Big Brother" and their ultrasound image.

The comments were flooded with congratulations from athletes and teams such as gymnast Simone Biles, Indiana Fever guard Caitlin Clark, New York Liberty forward Breanna Stewart, Los Angeles Sparks center Cameron Brink, San Francisco 49ers tight end George Kittle, the Fever and the Pacers.

Haliburton's current and former teammates Andrew Nembhard, James Johnson and Jay Huff also chimed in, as did the Golden State Warriors' Georges Niang and Charlotte Hornets' Grant Williams.

The post's caption reads: "Baby Hali. Spring 2027."

The Haliburtons wed in August after getting engaged in July 2025 and being together for seven years. The couple met while attending Iowa State. Jade was a cheerleader, and Tyrese played two seasons with the Cyclones before being drafted in 2020.

The Pacers guard tore his right Achilles tendon in Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals, sidelining him for all of the 2025-26 season. He returned this season and averaged 21.8 points, 9.5 assists and 4.5 rebounds in four games until suffering a hamstring strain that has kept him out since Oct. 26.

stories.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Arsenal, Newcastle eye Inter's Pio Esposito
stories.summary: Both Arsenal and Newcastle United are looking to improve their attack by signing Inter's Pio Esposito. Transfer Talk has the latest.
stories.body:
Arsenal and Newcastle United are competing to sign Internazionale striker Pio Esposito, while Bayern Munich's Luis Díaz and Chelsea's Estêvão are on the shortlist of UEFA Champions League winners Paris Saint-Germain. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Arsenal and Newcastle United are monitoring Internazionale striker Pio Esposito, according to Nicolo Schira. The Serie A club are reporrted to have turned down approaches worth around €60 million for the 21-year-old, who is contracted until 2032, and viewed as an indispensable member of manager Cristian Chivu's squad. Esposito scored a hat trick in the 4-4 league draw with Atalanta on Sunday and was also on target in both of Italy's Nations League clashes this month, as he scored a brace in the 3-1 win over France on Nov. 12.

- Paris Saint-Germain have added Bayern Munich's Luis Díaz and Chelsea's Estêvão to their shortlist, as they consider whether to strengthen their forward line following the long-term injuries sustained by Désiré Doué and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, according to Diario AS. PSG manager Luis Enrique wants to take time before making a decision, amid plans to assess the squad in the coming weeks, but the club have identified the 29-year-old Díaz as an option due to his direct dribbling style and Estêvão, 19, is also on the Ligue 1 club's radar due to his limited minutes in London.

- Chelsea are keeping tabs on Tottenham Hotspur winger Luca Williams-Barnett, who is closing in on signing a new contract, the Daily Telegraph reports. The Blues are watching the 18-year-old's situation alongside Borussia Dortmund, but Spurs are reportedly now handling the final details on an extension which could ward off interest in his signature. Williams-Barnett registered a goal and an assist on his first Premier League start in the 2-0 win over Ipswich Town on Saturday.

- Manchester United are preparing an approach for United States and Villarreal right back Alex Freeman, Football Insider reports. Scouts are reported to have been impressed by the 22-year-old's performances on multiple occasions, and the Red Devils have made him one of their top priorities for January in a move that would see him reunite with former USMNT manager Mauricio Pochettino. Freeman has made 16 appearances for the Yellow Submarine this season, continuing form since impressing at the 2026 World Cup in the summer.

- Bayern Munich are considering an approach for New York Red Bulls striker Eric Maxim Choupo-Moting, Sky Germany reports. The Bundesliga club are keen to acquire a short-term replacement for Harry Kane, who is set to be sidelined for several months following a ligament tear. Choupo-Moting, 37, is expected to be available as a free agent at the end of the year when his contract expires in Major League Soccer, and he is seen as a strong option due to his familiarity with the club. He directly contributed to 51 goals in 122 matches during a four-year spell at the Allianz Arena which ended in 2024.

stories.headline: WNBA players elect Elizabeth Williams as union president
stories.summary: Sky center Elizabeth Williams was elected president of the Women's National Basketball Players Association and will replace Nneka Ogwumike, who had been in the role since 2016.
stories.body:
Chicago Sky center Elizabeth Williams was elected president of the Women's National Basketball Players Association and will replace Nneka Ogwumike, who retired after being in the role since 2016.

Williams, who will serve out the final two years of Ogwumike's term that began earlier this year, was picked by players on Tuesday over Breanna Stewart of the New York Liberty and Gabby Williams of the Golden State Valkyries, a source with knowledge of the ballot told ESPN.

A 12-year veteran, Williams joined the WNBPA executive committee in 2018 and served four two-year terms. She has been at the bargaining table for two CBAs, including the most recent agreement that raised maximum player salaries to over $1 million.

"One of my main goals as president is to increase the engagement of the younger members of this union," Williams said in a statement to WNBPA player representatives. "I know the value of diverse voices in these conversations. We may not always agree, but I want to make sure every player knows that her voice is being heard.

"This is the strength of our union. I am grateful for what we have accomplished over these last few years, and I'm excited about the potential for a new opportunity to serve."

The WNBA will also have a new face leading the league office as commissioner Cathy Engelbert is retiring at the end of the year. A search for her replacement is ongoing.

Williams will lead the executive committee comprised of Napheesa Collier (1st vice president), Veronica Burton (secretary), Chelsea Gray (treasurer), and three additional vice presidents: Alysha Clark, Ezi Magbegor, and Maya Caldwell.

Burton, Gray, Magbegor and Caldwell join the executive committee for the first time.

"These election results reflect the strength of our union and the power of player leadership," WNBPA executive director Terri Carmichael Jackson said in a statement. "Congratulations to Elizabeth and each of our newly elected and returning Executive Committee members, whose collective experience, diverse perspectives, and commitment will help guide the WNBPA into its next chapter.

"As we turn our focus to implementing our transformational CBA and building on the progress our members have fought so hard to achieve, our greatest strength remains our unity, our democratic process, and our unwavering commitment to one another."

Williams, who was selected fourth overall in the 2015 WNBA draft out of Duke and was the 2016 Most Improved Player, becomes president after a lengthy period of stability in union leadership.

Ogwumike, the outgoing WNBPA president, announced her WNBA retirement during the 2026 season. An 11-time All-Star and the 2016 MVP, Ogwumike has served as WNBPA president since 2016, presiding over two collective bargaining agreement negotiations and shaping the social justice activism that defined the player body during her tenure.

stories.headline: Lightning forward Conor Geekie out 4-5 months after undergoing shoulder surgery
stories.summary: Lightning forward Conor Geekie is expected to miss the next four to five months after undergoing shoulder surgery.
stories.body:
Tampa Bay Lightning forward Conor Geekie is expected to miss the next four to five months after undergoing shoulder surgery, the team said Tuesday.

Geekie skated 14 shifts for more than eight minutes of ice time on Nov. 14 against Detroit and finished that game but has missed the past two. He had surgery Monday, the team said. The 22-year-old has four goals and one assist this season.

The Lightning acquired Geekie from Utah at the 2024 draft as part of the return for two-time Stanley Cup-winning defenseman Mikhail Sergachev.

stories.headline: Navajo Stirling belts another former champ, moves up in rankings

stories.body:
If you've ever worn a UFC light heavyweight championship belt, watch out for Navajo Stirling.

His two most recent victories have come against former 205-pound champions, both knockouts. After a first-round finish of Jan Blachowicz in August, the New Zealander knocked out Jiří Procházka in Saturday's UFC Fight Night main event in Qatar.

As a result, Stirling leapfrogs Procházka in the ESPN divisional rankings, rising to No. 3 at light heavyweight. After his fourth straight knockout overall, Stirling (12-0) is right behind the division's champion, Carlos Ulberg, Stirling's training partner at City Kickboxing in Auckland. The No. 1 ranking belongs to former champion Magomed Ankalaev, who called out Stirling after Saturday's fight.

The weekend's UFC fights also led to changes in the featherweight and men's flyweight top 10s. Aljamain Sterling lost a 145-pound fight to Kevin Vallejos and drops four spots to No. 7, right below Vallejos. stories.headline: Fiona the hippo to be honored by FC Cincinnati with tifo after untimely death
stories.summary: FC Cincinnati will honor Cincinnati Zoo's famous hippo, Fiona, following her unexpected death last week.
stories.body:
FC Cincinnati will honor Fiona, the local hippo who became famous on social media, following her unexpected death last week.

The MLS side is planning to unveil a special tifo to pay tribute to Fiona prior to their MLS Cup playoff match against Nashville on Saturday.

Fiona was beloved by many in Cincinnati, Ohio, and around the world. Fiona died of health complications last Thursday following after she swallowed a child's knit cap that had landed in her enclosure at Cincinnati Zoo.

The Nile hippopotamus became a worldwide sensation when she was born in 2017 at the zoo. Fiona arrived six weeks premature and her chances of survival were low.

But she beat the odds to make it through and grew into a viral star.

In 2017, local ice cream chain Graeter's even released a limited-edition flavor inspired by Fiona. It was called "Chunky Chunky Hippo."

FC Cincinnati said Fiona "became a symbol of Cincinnati and captured hearts around the world."

During FC Cincinnati's 3-1 win over Orlando on the day of Fiona's death, defender Nick Hagglund dedicated his goal to the hippo by exclaiming "that's for Fiona" before mimicking her ears on the top of his head.

Fiona was also honored by other Cincinnati sports teams upon news of her death, including NFL team Cincinnati Bengals and MLB side Cincinnati Reds. They both posted tributes to the much-loved hippo on their social media accounts.

- Bengals, Reds pay tribute to Fiona the hippo after her death

- NFL Week 11 arrivals: Tee Higgins pays homage to Fiona the Hippo ahead of 'MNF'

Bengals wide receiver Tee Higgins even wore a Fiona sweater on Monday night before his team lost to the Washington Commanders.

FC Cincinnati will also make a donation for every fan in attendance at TQL Stadium to the Cincinnati Zoo & Botanical Garden in Fiona's memory.

Speaking about Fiona's death, the Cincinnati Zoo director Dave Jenike said: "Our animal care team was heroic in their efforts to save her. They did everything possible, but her body couldn't fight anymore.

"She was dearly loved by her Zoo family and countless others around the world. Her loss will be felt deeply by so many."

FC Cincinnati can progress to the Eastern Conference semifinal with a win over Nashville on Saturday.

The Qatar Grand Prix takes place under the floodlights at the Lusail Circuit. It is one of the most demanding on the calendar with long straights and sweeping high-speed corners coupled with intense heat and humidity, making conditions for the cars and drivers difficult.

It was originally built as a motorbike circuit before it joined the F1 calendar in 2021 on a 10-year contract. Qatar did not host a race in 2022 as they focused on the FIFA World Cup.

Weather forecast

The weather for the Qatar Grand Prix is forecast to be sunny with a gentle breeze across the weekend. It's a night race so conditions are dry with highs of 24°C on Sunday.

What happened last time out?

McLaren's Piastri pipped teammate Norris to pole position as the battle for the world title continued with two races remaining.

During the race, Red Bull's Verstappen benefited from a McLaren strategy error to win his seventh race of the season, taking the three-way title race to the season finale in Abu Dhabi.

Piastri was leading the race and Norris was running in third, but the Papaya team decided against pitting under the Safety Car. Piastri ended the race in second, with Norris in fourth.

Who will win this year?

Verstappen looked unstoppable in Las Vegas and will be targeting his fifth win of the season in Qatar.

Mercedes' Russell was well in the mix last time out but will be looking to respond after Verstappen said the Englishman was "so far below his level" as their feud intensified.

Both teams look strong, so the rivalry could well continue in Qatar. Drivers up and down the grid will also be limited to 27 laps on each set of tyres, which will play massively into teams' strategies.

Tensions between Ferrari teammates Hamilton and Charles Leclerc continue to heat up after boss Fred Vasseur labelled them "unmanageable."

Don't count out new world champion Kimi Antonelli who is always one to watch after an impressive season.

stories.headline: Price tag for Tassie's new AFL stadium goes up, again
stories.summary: The estimated cost of a new 23,000-seat waterfront venue, set to eventually become the home of the Tasmania Devils, has risen again.
stories.body:
Tasmania's new AFL stadium has suffered another cost blowout, causing the premier to break a promise to cap the state's spend as critics fear the end price will be far higher.

The cost estimate for the 23,000-seat roofed venue at Macquarie Point in Hobart has increased from $1.13 billion to $1.23 billion.

On top of the figure is $132 million for broader precinct infrastructure, project delivery costs of $183 million and unspecified contingencies, taking the total to $1.54 billion.

Premier Jeremy Rockliff previously pledged to cap Tasmania's contribution to the build at $875 million as part of a deal to get the project through parliament.

But he conceded on Tuesday the state would have to cover the slated $100 million increase via extra borrowings.

"The previous cost estimate, which we announced ... some 14 months ago, there's been a lot of water under the bridge since that point," Mr Rockliff said.

The premier confirmed the project wouldn't head back to parliament for the approval of the necessary extra funding, despite previous assurances it would.

The latest estimate reflects increases in the cost of construction, sustained high oil and materials prices, higher labour costs and its complexity, the state government said.

The stadium is expected to be ready for the 2031 AFL season and was a condition of the Tasmania Devils being granted a licence to enter into the national competition in 2028.

It initially had a price tag of $715 million.

Mr Rockliff said the state had reached out to the federal government and AFL for extra money on top of their $240 million and $15 million contributions.

Anti-stadium group Our Place Hobart said the new cost estimate failed to take into account other factors, including the interest bill and the exact cost of contingencies.

Greens leader Rosalie Woodruff described the ongoing cost increases as a deep betrayal of Tasmanians.

"Who knows where the final price for the stadium will end up?" she said.

"What we do know is there's been now a fifth major cost blowout and there's not yet a contract price locked in for this massive project."

Federal independent MP Andrew Wilkie fears the stadium will end up costing $2 billion.

"Once you add the cost of the debt over a decade, the total cost to the Tasmanian taxpayer is closer to $3.5 billion," he said.

Devils chief executive Brendon Gale said the question of any additional funding from the AFL was a matter for the sport's governing body.

"The politicians can politic. We'll get on with building our club," he said.

"People have their views and are entitled to them. But based on my experience, people never look back. These types of projects transform cities and states."

The release of updated costs came ahead of schedule after the government bowed to political pressure to make the figures public before the end of the parliamentary year.

In mid-October, BESIX Watpac was announced as the preferred builder. A final contract is set to be signed by the end of 2026.

BESIX Watpac recently built a 30,000-seat roofed stadium in Christchurch in New Zealand which cost about $540 million.

Mr Rockliff said the final contract price for the Hobart stadium was unlikely to differ from the $1.23 billion estimate.

The stadium has been deeply divisive in Tasmania amid rising state debt, a stretched health system and other under-pressure services.

The AFL and federal government have been contacted for comment.

stories.headline: 'Little disappointing': Munster makes call on Storm offer
stories.summary: Melbourne's fight to keep Cameron Munster and Harry Grant has been made harder after the former rejected the club's latest offer.
stories.body:
Cameron Munster has declared all options are on the table after officially rejecting a deal to stay in Melbourne and labelling the Storm's latest offer as "disappointing".

With Melbourne already facing a battle to retain Harry Grant, the Storm are now officially fighting a retention war on two fronts after Munster's call.

The Melbourne superstar admitted on Tuesday that Grant's future could play a role in his own call, as well as Craig Bellamy's impending retirement at the end of 2027.

As it stands Munster will not take up an offer from the Storm that is understood to have been for one year with an option for a second.

"I have declined it," the Queensland State of Origin captain said at a Maroons sponsor announcement with Westpac.

"I am not saying I am going to leave Melbourne. Just with the terms and conditions that they put out to me, it is probably something that is a little disappointing.

"But it's a business, I am not stupid."

Munster admitted his own form had not been good enough for the Storm last season as they missed the finals for the first time in his career.

And in turn, the 32-year-old conceded the offer may have been as a result of that.

"That (offer) just makes my job a little bit harder. But it's also a bit of a challenge saying I am not where I need to be," he said.

"Maybe I need to be a little bit better to earn that contract that we're looking from.

"And maybe it is a little bit of a kick up the bum from them. I am not too sure where we'll go from here but all options are open at the moment."

Munster's rejection comes after Grant met with Gold Coast officials last Friday and officially received an offer to join the Titans.

It is understood Melbourne's offer for the Queensland dummy-half will either be worth similar or more than the Titans.

But Gold Coast are hopeful of luring the hooker north, given his relationship with ex-Maroons assistant coach Josh Hannay and prop Tino Fa'asuamaleaui.

The Titans officially released AJ Brimson to the PNG Chiefs on Tuesday on a three-year deal, with the money from the centre used to help pursue Grant.

NSW prop Stefano Utoikamanu is also off contract at Melbourne at the end of next year and has also been linked to the Sydney Roosters.

At the same time Bellamy's retirement at the end of next season is proving a challenge for the Storm, given he is like a father figure to Munster.

"When you look at someone like Craig as a coach, he is a great coach and I have so much respect and have admired him for such a long time," Munster said.

"It's going to be different at the club. I'm not too sure where the club wants to go with all that stuff.

"I don't know who they are going to get and I'm sure it will be a daunting job coming after him."

Munster also confirmed he will likely follow the Cameron Smith route and give away representative football at some point to focus on club duties.

"It definitely has (crossed my mind)," Munster said.

"The hard thing for me is giving up the captaincy.

"Once I start declining (I will look at it) and I thought I was declining. But after my last few games for the World Cup I am pretty confident I can get back to that."

stories.headline: Bellingham credits Mourinho 'full stop' for stellar form after Madrid stunner
stories.summary: Jude Bellingham praised José Mourinho for helping him reach career-best form after the midfielder scored a stunning goal in Real Madrid's 5-1 comeback win over PSV Eindhoven on Tuesday.
stories.body:
Jude Bellingham praised José Mourinho for helping him reach career-best form after the midfielder scored a stunning goal in Real Madrid's 5-1 comeback win over PSV Eindhoven on Tuesday.

Madrid trailed 1-0 at halftime before Mourinho made a triple substitution -- including the introduction of Bellingham -- and the home side then dominated, with Kylian Mbappé netting a brace, and Vinícius Júnior scoring his first Champions League goal this season.

Madrid are now top of the league phase table with 15 points after winning all five UCL matches so far, with a visit to Arsenal in their next European game on Dec. 9.

"Mourinho. Full stop," Bellingham told journalists at the Bernabéu, when asked to explain his outstanding form, with four goals in his last five club games. "I'm enjoying my football a lot. I love the coach, his staff, and my teammates help me a lot.

"That's why I'm playing well, because I have a lot of help."

Bellingham was asked if his displays with England at the World Cup -- where he scored seven goals playing behind Harry Kane -- had been the catalyst for his renewed goal threat.

"I don't know if it's because I'm playing as a number 10, it's having freedom," Bellingham said. " Freedom to move, to drop deep, to help build up, and to play higher up to finish.

"I think Mourinho has given me a lot of confidence. That's why I'm playing well, because I'm happy."

Madrid have now beaten Inter Milan, Roma, RB Leipzig, AEK Athens and PSV in the Champions League this season, despite some inconsistent performances.

"The second half was a question of mentality," Mourinho told Movistar. "We made changes, and Jude is a different player. He gives us what we didn't have in the first [half].

"It was a mental 'click.' In the first half we didn't find our rhythm, we didn't press, we didn't win duels."

Mourinho refused to reveal if he'd been angry with his players in the dressing room at halftime.

"The dressing room is like Vegas," the coach said. "What happens in Vegas, stays in Vegas.

"We spoke. We're friends, and we spoke."

"Once again, the first half wasn't good," goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois said. "In modern football, if we don't all run and do what the manager asks of us, it's impossible, especially against a team that presses you man-to-man.

"With the clips [Mourinho] showed us on the screen at halftime, you could see we weren't doing things right. That changed our attitude."

Madrid, who are three points behind LaLiga leaders Barcelona, next play Alaves at the Bernabeu on Nov. 28.

stories.headline: Brandon Aiyuk scheduled for visit Wednesday with Commanders, agent says
stories.summary: Wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk is scheduled to visit Wednesday with the Commanders, agent Drew Rosenhaus told ESPN's Adam Schefter.
stories.body:
Wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk is scheduled to visit Wednesday with the Washington Commanders, agent Drew Rosenhaus told ESPN's Adam Schefter.

The San Francisco 49ers released Aiyuk on Tuesday, two weeks after the NFL reinstated him. He cleared waivers, making him an unrestricted free agent.

Aiyuk has not played since tearing the ACL, MCL and meniscus in his right knee on Oct. 20, 2024, and was placed on the 49ers' reserve/left squad list last December. He could not be removed from that list until he reported and passed a physical, which he did Nov. 9.

"I'm feeling great, feeling healthy," Aiyuk told 49ers reporters earlier this month. "It was a long recovery process, a long rehab process, but I'm back to 100%."

Aiyuk is expected to work out for the Commanders during Wednesday's visit.

In 2023, his last full season before his injury, Aiyuk was named second-team All-Pro after catching 75 passes for 1,342 yards and seven touchdowns.

Aiyuk and Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels played together at Arizona State during the 2019 season. However, a rift in their relationship appeared to have developed following a series of social media posts by the receiver. Aiyuk targeted Daniels in several posts and in one referenced Daniels' mother.

Daniels and Aiyuk spoke more than a month ago to clear the air, according to multiple sources.

Daniels befriended Aiyuk early in their time together at ASU -- before Daniels had won the starting quarterback job. During workouts, Daniels would throw with Aiyuk, who was going into his senior season and coming off a 33-catch, 474-yard season.

They quickly developed a rapport as Aiyuk ended the season with Associated Press All-America honors after catching 65 passes for 1,192 yards and eight touchdowns.

ESPN's John Keim contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Fantasy baseball reactions to MLB offseason trades, signings
stories.summary: Track all the latest MLB free agency and trade news with fantasy baseball analysis from Tristan H. Cockcroft and Eric Karabell.
stories.byline: Tristan H. Cockcroft and Eric Karabell
stories.body:
Tracking the offseason MLB trades and signings with fantasy baseball implications for the upcoming season, Eric Karabell and Tristan H. Cockcroft will analyze and provide an outlook for all of the key players involved.

Players were allowed to sign with new teams beginning Nov. 2, although typically things don't really start to heat up until the league's annual winter meetings. This year's meetings are scheduled to take place in San Diego from Dec. 7-9. However, with the current collective bargaining agreement expiring Dec. 1, players and teams alike might end up waiting until after the dust settles on negotiations and a potential lockout before inking any new deals.

In any event, as any contracts are signed or trades get agreed to, this is the place to find all of the fantasy fallout of those deals. Be sure to check back throughout the hot stove season for updates. Latest updates include the Toronto Blue Jays signing Japanese star Kaima Taira, the Chicago Cubs signing both Trevor Rogers and Teroaki Sato and Freddy Peralta signing with the Baltimore Orioles.

Below, you will find a list of some of the top free agents at each position. Players labeled with a (Q) received a qualifying offer from their current team and had until Nov. 17 to accept it or decline and become a free agent. Players coming from Japan/Korea who were posted by their current team have a Dec. 1 deadline to reach a deal with an MLB club to play in the United States in 2027.

Note: Not every transaction warrants the attention of fantasy managers, but for those signings and trades that do merit analysis, you'll find them listed below. Players will be separated by position and then listed in chronological order of the move within each positional grouping, with the latest news coming first. Also included are links to any standalone analysis stories and/or videos regarding major free agent signings and trades. Players who end up re-signing with their previous team will not always be included.

Jump to:

Catcher | First base | Second base | Shortstop | Third base

Outfield | DH | Starting pitcher | Relief pitcher

Catcher
Some free agents: Carson Kelly, Tyler Stephenson, Kyle Higashioka, Gary Sanchez, James McCann, Travis d'Arnaud, Austin Hedges

First base
Paul Goldschmidt signs with Mets
Goldschmidt, 39, hit only .252 over 380 PA with the Yankees last season -- but how he did so explains why the Mets coveted him. Goldschmidt hit .299/.393/.573 with 11 home runs versus left-handed pitching, one year after posting a .336/.411/.570 line. He has not enjoyed recent success against right-handed pitching. The Mets figure to platoon Goldschmidt, perhaps with lefty-hitting Jared Young. While that should be productive for the team, it isn't so great for fantasy managers.

Goldschmidt finished outside the top 50 first basemen in 2026 scoring. Roster him in daily formats, when you can take advantage of knowing exactly when he will be in the lineup. Fade him in standard leagues. -- Karabell (11/23)

Jake Bauers signs with Red Sox
Bauers, 31, comes off the best season of his journeyman career, posting an .873 OPS with 26 homers and 86 RBIs for the World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers. He admits that he considered retirement as recently as two years ago, but he stuck around for the health benefits. Good timing. Bauers gets a four-year deal with the Red Sox, where he and right-handed-hitting Willson Contreras should make for a formidable 1-2 punch in the middle of the lineup, while sharing 1B/DH duties.

While Bauers was a top-40 hitter in points formats and roto/categories leagues last season, fantasy managers probably shouldn't expect the same kind of production moving forward, even as he performs half the time at hitter-friendly Fenway Park. Bauers had never hit more than 12 home runs in any prior season and, even now, he remains a career .223 hitter with a 2.0 career WAR.

Maybe the solid 16.3% walk rate and .218 ISO will continue, but preliminary results in NFBC drafts have Bauers going just inside the top 150. Perhaps he gets a bump for heading to Boston, but likely only a modest one. -- Karabell (11/13)

Other free agents: Josh Bell, Ryan Mountcastle, Nathaniel Lowe, Ty France

Second base

Some free agents: Gleyber Torres, Jeff McNeil, Luis Arraez, Jazz Chisholm Jr., Jonathan India, Gavin Lux, Brandon Lowe (Q)

Shortstop

Some free agents: Ha-Seong Kim, J.P. Crawford, Mauricio Dubon, Isiah Kiner-Falefa, Amed Rosario

Third base
Teruaki Sato signs with Cubs
Sato, 27 and the defending Nippon Central League Triple Crown winner, reminds many of another left-handed hitting Japanese slugger who came to the United States. Chicago White Sox 1B Munetaka Murakami, who, in his first MLB season, launched 35 home runs with a 16.6% walk rate, albeit with a .207 batting average and 35.4% strikeout rate. Sato is viewed as a better athlete, but expected to offer a similar offensive profile in the "three true outcomes" department, with power, walks and strikeouts.

This profile has value in fantasy, but Murakami averaged only 2.1 ESPN fantasy points per game, outside the top 100 hitters. He was the No. 127 hitter on the Player Rater, even though only nine hitters slugged more home runs. Should potential Sato investors expect better numbers than Murakami's debut? Sato may boast better plate discipline and a better likelihood to adjust his approach, perhaps trading some power for better contact. Fangraphs projects a .247 batting average and 30 home runs. While Murakami is not among ESPN's initial top 200 for points formats, Sato should earn a better ranking, though not among the top 100.

Though Sato is likely ticketed for an outfield corner with the Cubs, he will be eligible at third base only in fantasy drafts based on his games played in Japan in 2026. He can earn additional eligibility with 10 games played at another position in 2027. -- Karabell (11/24)

Royce Lewis traded to Dodgers
Lewis, 27 and a former first-round pick of the Twins in 2017, has long been ticketed for slugging stardom, but his road to becoming one of the premier, power-hitting third basemen has been bumpy. Lewis hit 15 home runs and knocked in 52 over 58 games and 239 PA during his breakout 2023 campaign, with a .920 OPS. Injuries have derailed him since, as Lewis has neither reached 20 home runs in a season nor approached a .800 OPS.

At least Lewis managed to stay healthy enough to reach 500 PA for the first time in 2026, though he struck out in 25.5% of his PA with a career-low 71.9% contact rate. Can the Los Angeles Dodgers get him consistently productive and keep him on the field? The Minnesota Twins clearly could not. Eligible at first base and third base, perhaps the Dodgers view Lewis as a utility option and lefty killer, but if he doesn't hit, it doesn't matter. Bump Lewis up your draft sheets a bit because of this trade, but he remains more of a late-round sleeper than a sure thing. -- Karabell 11/20

Maikel Garcia traded to Mariners
Garcia, 26, suffered through a rough 2026 season, missing months with hamstring and hand injuries, and slugging only .381 during his 82 games and 344 PA. Not that Garcia is a renowned power hitter, but he delivered 16 home runs among his 60 extra-base hits in a breakout 2025, along with 23 stolen bases, after stealing 37 bases in 2024. Garcia missed only seven games during 2024-25, so volume played a role when he finished 18th among hitters in 2025 fantasy points.

A 2025 Gold Glove winner, Garcia is one of the better defensive third basemen in baseball, and he should solidify the position for Seattle. However, while we don't know for sure where he will hit in his new lineup -- and leaving one hitter-challenging home ballpark in Kansas City for another does not help him -- it figures to be near the bottom half, which caps his fantasy upside. Expect Garcia to bounce back to some degree offensively, with his early ESPN 2027 points ranking featuring him positively as the No. 10 3B and just outside the top 100. -- Karabell (11/18)

Some free agents: Alec Bohm, Eugenio Suarez, Edmundo Sosa, Yoan Moncada, Si Hwan Roh (posted)

Outfield

Some free agents: George Springer, Trent Grisham, Ian Happ, Seiya Suzuki (Q), Randy Arozarena, Taylor Ward, Daulton Varsho, Adolis Garcia, Luis Robert Jr., Randal Grichuk, Myles Straw, Lane Thomas

Designated hitter

Some free agents: Joc Pederson, Dominic Smith

Starting pitcher
Tarik Skubal signs with Mets
Two winters ago, the New York Mets opened their wallet to get their offensive centerpiece, Juan Soto. On Sunday, the Mets did the same to get a centerpiece for their rotation, and for a similarly record-setting deal, signing Tarik Skubal to a nine-year, $450 million contract.

Fortunately for us in fantasy, we won't need to spend as much as the Mets did to add Skubal to our rosters, but it's a good landing spot for the lefty. He'll call one of the more pitching-leaning ballparks in Citi Field his home through 2036. -- Cockcroft (11/23)

For a more in-depth look at the fantasy impact of Skubal's signing, click here.

Toronto Blue Jays sign SP Kaima Taira

Having missed out on their top free-agent pitching prize, Tarik Skubal, the Blue Jays moved quickly to sign Taira, who by many accounts had the second-best raw stuff of any pitcher on this winter's market, to a five-year, $80 million contract. Taira spent seven of his first eight seasons in Japan as a reliever but transitioned beautifully to a starting pitching role in 2026, posting a Nippon Professional Baseball-leading 1.36 ERA across 22 starts and one relief appearance. Prior to that, he had posted sub-2 ERAs in each of his prior five seasons working out of the bullpen (2020-22, '24-25), 31 saves in 2025, as well as a 2.40 ERA in 23 starts while pitching out of the rotation in 2023.

That's a remarkable level of success for a pitcher who stands just 5-foot-8. Marcus Stroman is the only MLB pitcher this century who stood that height or shorter to have made as many as 10 starts. Taira's extension -- measuring the distance from the pitching rubber that the pitcher releases the baseball -- is regarded as elite, however, and to a point where he'd likely rank in the upper quarter in U.S. play in that department. Between that and his six -- and, by some accounts, as many as eight -- pitches in his repertoire, he counters the height question with a great deal of upside. Taira's command of his pitch mix is considered elite, and generally ground ball-generating, so even with some anticipated regression to his strikeout rate he might well deliver numbers that place among the top 40 pitchers in fantasy baseball.

We'll see how swiftly and smoothly Taira adapts to U.S. play, which despite becoming less demanding upon starting pitchers in the post-COVID era, still has a lengthier and more physically taxing schedule. Questions about whether he's more suited for relief than rotation work are valid, and the primary obstacle towards him earning that potential top-40 starter ranking. By signing in Toronto, where he's more likely to have the team's patience with his adapting to the rotation, Saito will earn a ranking around No. 75 at the position, in the Joey Cantillo/Trey Yesavage/Eduardo Rodriguez range. -- Cockcroft (11/24)

RHP Freddy Peralta signs with Orioles

Peralta, 30, ended the 2026 season with a bloated 4.42 ERA and 1.33 WHIP, but those numbers hardly tell the story. The longtime Brewers ace who struck out 200 hitters during three consecutive seasons started the 2026 season with the Mets after an offseason trade, and things went poorly right away. Then, months later, the Mets traded Peralta to the Rays and, voila, all was well again!

With his mechanics tweaked and his approach refined (more changeups, fewer sliders), Peralta posted a 3.25 ERA and 1.01 WHIP during 10 Rays starts, albeit with a lower strikeout rate than typical, but at least he was good. Then he thrived in the postseason, winning ALCS MVP honors. That is what fantasy managers expect. Peralta may not be a top 20 starting pitcher for fantasy, but he should be close. Peralta ranks among the top 100 players for points and roto formats. -- Karabell (11/24)

LHP Trevor Rogers signs with Cubs
Rogers, 29, was never going to match his incredible 2025 season, when he posted a 1.81 ERA and 0.90 WHIP during 18 starts, but his 2026 campaign (4.03, 1.18) may have still exceeded some expectations. After all, the 6-foot-5 left-hander posted a 4.92 ERA and 1.58 WHIP for the Marlins and Orioles in 2024. The 2017 first-round pick dealt with injuries, control issues and inconsistency for much of his career, among other things. Then, suddenly, he was a star, even for half a season.

Rogers probably isn't a star. The Cubs get a guy who made 30 starts (for the first time) and did his best work in the second half, with a 3.52 ERA and 1.04 WHIP, whiffing 27% of hitters. That's good, reliable work, and Rogers was among the top 40 starting pitchers in ESPN fantasy points. Can the Cubs and fantasy managers get that version in 2027? That seems reasonable. Rogers isn't an ace, but worthy of being among the top 40 starters in drafts. There is nothing wrong with that. --Karabell (11/24)

Luis Castillo and Davis Martin traded to Rockies
What happens when the league's worst non-Rockies or Athletics pitcher (minimum 130 innings) comes to Coors Field? We're about to find out. Castillo entered 2026 riding a four-year streak with at least 350 fantasy points, 160 strikeouts and a sub-1.20 WHIP. However, a progressive drop in his velocity and a rise in his fly ball rate during that time caused him to unravel last year, first for the Seattle Mariners and then catastrophically so following his midseason trade to the Chicago White Sox. Castillo's year ended with a shoulder injury, so in addition to the Coors factor, he enters 2027 facing many questions.

Martin, meanwhile, was the far superior fantasy pitcher between these two -- by almost two times in terms of point production (242-127). Martin, though, ended 2026 on a similarly sour note. He had a 9-2 record and 2.41 ERA through his first 13 starts, but went 0-8 with a 5.72 ERA thereafter. He dealt with a calf issue, a blister and concerns that he might be tipping pitches, ultimately making only a mop-up appearance during Chicago's playoff run.

Martin was nevertheless the piece the Rockies wanted in order to agree to absorb Castillo's remaining contract. Both will probably eat innings for a Rockies rotation always in need of depth. Either could be a "matchup candidate" in road games, if they seem to have righted the ship during spring training -- which is why a lockout-influenced, shortened preseason would be detrimental to both. Still, neither pitcher is a draft-day option, given their new team. -- Cockcroft (11/20)

Twins sign SP Sonny Gray
Gray, now 37 years old, returns to Minnesota after a three-year detour through St. Louis and Boston. He has enjoyed a bit of a career rebirth later in his career, averaging 385.8 fantasy points over the past four seasons, and never deviating by more than 25 points in either direction in any individual year. Gray's consistency is a valuable thing in fantasy leagues, particularly points-based scoring, where his good ratios and solid innings totals are most advantageous.

That said, a two-year pattern of declining average fastball velocity and strikeout rates raises concerns that regression might hit him harder than a typical frontline starter, if not in 2027 then perhaps if he doesn't opt out and continues into his 39-year-old campaign in 2028. I've got Gray ranked amongst my top 25 fantasy starting pitchers, and within the top 75 overall, and I'd expect he will (and should) generally be drafted in that range.

Gray's acquisition, however, gives the Twins at least nine viable rotation candidates, creating a logjam of popular deep-mixed/AL-only names like Mick Abel, Zebby Matthews, Connor Prielipp for fourth/fifth starter spots. Perhaps a trade is forthcoming, preferably for some hitting to bolster the lineup and give Gray more run support, but otherwise this is a spring battle that'll be high on the list of those to watch. Only Gray, Joe Ryan, Taj Bradley and Pablo Lopez would figure to be locks. -- Cockcroft (11/18)

Bryce Miller traded to Royals
Miller, 28, emerged as a standout fantasy option for the Seattle Mariners in 2024, winning 12 games and posting a 2.94 ERA and 0.98 WHIP. Injuries and inconsistency have plagued the right-hander since then, as Miller won only eight of 39 starts in 2025-26 with a 4.82 ERA and 1.26 WHIP while permitting 38 home runs. Elbow woes ruined his 2025 campaign, and he missed the first six weeks of 2026 with an oblique injury.

Still, when Miller is healthy, he can be effective. He posted a 2.18 ERA and 0.83 WHIP prior to the 2026 All-Star break before a rough second half (and myriad home runs) ruined things. Moving from one pitcher's park in Seattle to another in Kansas City shouldn't be a factor, but at least Miller should be guaranteed a rotation spot, which was in question in Seattle. Miller is certainly a sleeper candidate to regain his place among the top 30 starting pitchers in fantasy, but ESPN's preliminary points ranking features Miller well outside the top 50 starting pitchers. -- Karabell (11/18)

Dustin May signs with White Sox
May, 29, made 31 mostly league-average starts for the Cardinals and eventual champion Brewers this season -- many of them quite abbreviated. In fact, he ended up averaging fewer than four innings over his 10 Brewers starts and he did not qualify for the ERA title. The desperate White Sox figure to allow May to go deeper into games, but that comes at a cost, since he posted a 4.70 ERA and a 1.32 WHIP with only 0.4 bWAR last season.

Hey, at least May stayed healthy, which is a feat for him. Plus, he was a bit unlucky, as his 3.54 FIP indicates. However, that doesn't mean May warrants inclusion in ESPN standard drafts, with a preliminary points-league rank outside the top 75 starting pitchers. -- Karabell (11/18)

Other free agents: Michael King, Robbie Ray, Brandon Woodruff, Zac Gallen, Shota Imanaga, Kevin Gausman, Chris Bassitt, Jack Flaherty, Jameson Taillon, Max Scherzer, Clay Holmes, Matthew Boyd, Nick Pivetta, Shane Bieber, Nick Martinez, Tyler Mahle, Foster Griffin, Michael Soroka

Relief pitcher
RHP Emilio Pagan signs with Tigers
Pagan, 35, saved 57 games for the Cincinnati Reds over the past two seasons, although his 2025 numbers were rather ordinary (3.38 ERA, 25.9% K rate). Still, this is a franchise that desired Kenley Jansen and let him save 22 games last season even though there were better pitchers in the bullpen. Pagan produced nearly identical stats to Jansen. In other words, Pagan isn't so valuable -- but if all you care about are saves in a roto format, a healthy Pagan should provide at least 25 of them. -- Karabell (11/13)

RHP Evan Phillips signs with Braves
Phillips, 32, posted a 2.36 ERA over parts of six seasons for the Los Angeles Dodgers. He also accrued 42 combined saves during 2023 and 2024. He missed most of 2025 dealing with Tommy John surgery and returned last season to pitch 26 effective innings. Additionally, Phillips has never permitted a run over 18⅓ postseason innings. The Braves figure to turn to RHP Robert Suarez to close (because Raisel Iglesias is a free agent), but a healthy Phillips should accrue ample holds as well as occasional saves. -- Karabell (11/13)

Other free agents: Raisel Iglesias, Pete Fairbanks, Carlos Estevez, A.J. Minter, Blake Treinen, Martin Perez, Gregory Soto, Kenley Jansen, Hiromi Itoh (posted)

stories.headline: Tracy Morgan reveals how he kept Knicks' title celebration ticking
stories.summary: Morgan also discussed in an appearance on "Live with Kelly and Mark" his experience traveling to Knicks road playoff games -- seven private jets and all.
stories.body:
In addition to their championship rings, New York Knicks players received an additional form of bling after their NBA Finals win -- courtesy of Tracy Morgan.

In a Tuesday appearance on "Live with Kelly and Mark," Morgan revealed that he made sure the team received a special -- and expensive -- token of his appreciation for the joy their title brought him and New York City.

And it wasn't just the players who benefited from Morgan's gift.

"After they won the championship I bought the whole team, Dolan, the coaches, I bought them all Rolexes," Morgan said, to gasps from the studio audience.

Morgan also spoke about Knicks fandom in the city at large, and the passion of the team's supporters -- as well as their willingness to travel.

"We got a fanbase here in New York, our fanbase needs to be studied and observed," Morgan said. "Because we move.

"My boy Al Palagonia, he usually sits with Spike Lee, he owns a private jet company. We would take seven jets, every away game. Seven jets. And we would go, and the tickets, we would pay like, 45,000 a ticket, and we would sit right behind our team. And we were part of it."

And, as Morgan pointed out, he never had to worry about talking trash on the road -- because the Knicks celebrity contingent would never be the only New York fans in the building. Sometimes, they were the majority in the stands.

"Nah, it was 60-40 New York, we wasn't worried about none of that," Morgan said. "This is New York, this is where King Kong died. And we told Godzilla, 'You next. You, the three-headed monster, the flying turtle, all y'all can get it.'"

stories.headline: Man United win appeal over Leny Yoro red card
stories.summary: Manchester United defender Leny Yoro's one-match suspension has been removed following a successful claim of wrongful dismissal.
stories.body:
Manchester United have won their appeal over Leny Yoro's red card against Liverpool.

The Frenchman was dismissed after eight minutes at Anfield after a challenge on Alexander Isak. On-field referee Sam Barrott decided Yoro had denied a clear goalscoring opportunity, a view backed up by VAR John Brooks.

United, who lost 4-0 in Mauricio Pochettino's first game as head coach, launched an appeal on Monday, insisting that Isak's heavy touch meant he would not have had the chance to score.

The Football Association announced on Tuesday that the claim of wrongful dismissal has been upheld and Yoro's one-match ban has been lifted.

A statement issued by the FA read: "Leny Yoro's one-match suspension has been removed following a successful claim of wrongful dismissal.

"The Manchester United player was sent off for denying an obvious goal scoring opportunity during their Premier League match against Liverpool on Sunday Nov. 22."

Bruno Fernandes: Leny Yoro foul 'never a red card'

Bruno Fernandes told the BBC that it was "never a red card," adding: "I think it's too many referees on the pitch and too many on VAR, seated, with such a long time to see and put it back, go forward, put it back, do it in slow motion, whatsoever.

"To make a mistake like this can change a game. But obviously, then, it's not because of them that we concede the goal from the free-kick, but it changes completely the flow of the game."

Pochettino said: "I wasn't agreeing with the red card because I think the situation was when Isak control the ball, the ball wasn't in his control."

Kobbie Mainoo added: "The ball is already with the keeper when he's gone down, two players running at full speed. I mean, it's impossible to be a red, but it is what it is."

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola defended the referee's decision, saying: "[Yoro] is clearly the last man, it is clearly a foul. Would Alex or the 'keeper arrive first to the ball? We will never know. It's a clear foul, he's a last player, Alex goes against the 'keeper."

It's the second major refereeing error in a game involving United this season. In September, referee's body Pro Ref apologised after Erling Haaland's goal at Old Trafford was mistakenly allowed to stand.

City, who were reduced to 10 men in the first half after Phil Foden's red card, won the game 1-0.

stories.headline: Caitlin Clark says playing Augusta for the first time on 'bucket list'
stories.summary: During the WNBA offseason, Caitlin Clark said it's on her "bucket list" to play at Augusta for the first time.
stories.body:
Caitlin Clark heads into the WNBA offseason with golf on her mind, specifically one course. She has never played the home of the Masters.

"I want to play Augusta for the first time," Clark said on the "New Heights" podcast with Jason and Travis Kelce. "I haven't played there yet. I have a couple of opportunities to do that, so I'm looking forward to that. That's probably on my bucket list."

She said she has a 15 handicap index and that she's hitting her drives in the 230-yard range, giving her a wedge into most greens when she's playing the forward tees.

Clark said she recently played The Grove XXIII in Florida owned by Michael Jordan, which she called "not very challenging." That was intended as a compliment.

"It's like a fun, good hang course, where you actually feel good about golfing," Clark said. "Some of these places are so challenging it's not even fun."

Stay tuned for her take on Augusta National.

stories.headline: Lewis Hamilton: I could have beaten Kimi Antonelli if I was Ferrari No. 1
stories.summary: Lewis Hamilton has said he believes he could have won a record eighth world championship this season if Ferrari had prioritised him over teammate Charles Leclerc.
stories.body:
Lewis Hamilton has said he believes he could have won a record eighth world championship this season if Ferrari had prioritised him over teammate Charles Leclerc.

Hamilton's claim arrived after he tangled with Leclerc for the second time in three races at the Las Vegas Grand Prix -- a flashpoint Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur described as "completely unacceptable." Leclerc was sanctioned by the stewards for his role in the collision.

Hamilton's maiden win for Ferrari at the seventh round of 23 in Barcelona took him 41 points behind Antonelli, and 40 ahead of Leclerc.

And although Hamilton rejected the notion that he ever called on Ferrari to make him its number one driver, the 41-year-old suggested that, with the right backing from his team, he could have afforded Antonelli a proper run for his money.

"I've never asked to be the number one," Hamilton said. "I genuinely haven't. But there was a point in the season where I was 40 points ahead [of Leclerc] and at that point, the fight was with me and Kimi.

"I was the closest one to him. I was second for a long time in the year, and at that point I needed the backing to make sure we beat Kimi.

"There were a few instances in the season -- where, with the support -- I think we could have beaten Kimi in that battle.

"It's not what I've asked for. But we shouldn't have been able to come together [in Las Vegas]. It should just never happen. I've said everything I can on it. And the question now should be for Ferrari."

Hamilton's chances of finishing runner-up in the standings -- his highest championship position since missing out on his eighth title to Max Verstappen in 2021 -- now look shot following the Dutch driver's brilliant recent form.

- Lewis Hamilton, Charles Leclerc 'unmanageable' - Ferrari boss

- Max Verstappen, George Russell's latest war of words unlikely to stay in Vegas

- Max Verstappen mocks George Russell in brutal outburst: 'So far below my level'

Hamilton is 37 points behind Verstappen with only 50 points left across the remaining rounds, in Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

Hamilton is three points clear of both George Russell and Lando Norris, with Leclerc 17 points adrift.

Russell finished only ninth in Sin City after he pranged the barriers with just two laps remaining when a late move on teammate Antonelli for second backfired.

"I wanted that win," Russell said. "It was a bizarre race, and I went for a high-risk move and paid the price.

"Of course I'm disappointed with the outcome, however, I have no regrets. I fought and knew if I wanted the win, I needed to be in the top two positions into the final laps."

stories.headline: Heeney headlines returning Swans at pre-season training
stories.summary: After months of off-field turmoil in the fallout from the Pullman Hotel scandal, the Sydney Swans have welcomed back four AFL players for pre-season training.
stories.body:
The Sydney Swans have welcomed back their embattled AFL quartet to training after months of off-field turmoil following the Pullman Hotel scandal.

Isaac Heeney, Chad Warner, James Jordon and Riley Bice signalled their intent to resurrect their playing careers by taking part in the club's first-to-fourth-year pre-season training on Monday.

High-profile forward Tom Papley was also in attendance at Sydney's Bat and Ball Oval after being slapped with a three-game ban by the AFL for a positive roadside drug test.

Monday's session marked the first time Heeney, Warner, Bice and Jordon have officially trained with the Swans since serving a season-ending suspension for what the club termed a "serious breach of expected club behaviour and standards".

That AFL-endorsed suspension was also served by now-North Melbourne player Nick Blakey.

Separate from the bans, Heeney, Warner, Jordon and Blakey were under investigation after three women made reports of sexual assault to Victoria Police.

Police have since confirmed the players would not be charged due to insufficient evidence.

Civil claims are still being prepared against relevant parties.

Monday's session was a relaxed affair, with the club also welcoming draftees Caylen Murray, Mason McGroder, Mitchell Knevitt and Brady Wright.

Players undertook the usual pre-season conditioning programs, doing running drills before moving on to contest work and a short match simulation.

It wasn't the first time Heeney, Warner, Jordon and Rice had trained with teammates, having done informal sessions at Centennial Park.

Papley, one of the team's most experienced players, returned to training as he prepares to face Waverley Local Court for driving with a suspended licence on November 26.

The 30-year-old was pulled over by NSW Police for a random roadside drug test on November 2, with checks revealing his licence was suspended due to non-payment of a parking fine.

The initial roadside test returned a positive reading, and a secondary sample of oral fluid was taken.

That secondary sample returned a positive roadside test for the presence of cocaine and MDMA.

On top of his AFL ban for conduct unbecoming, Papley was fined $722 by police and his licence will be suspended for three months.

Papley spent most of Monday's training session with the rehabilitation group alongside fellow forwards Logan McDonald and Hayden McLean after undergoing surgery on both knees.

He suffered a grade-two medial collateral ligament strain in his right knee in the club's preliminary final loss to Fremantle, before undergoing an arthroscopy on his left knee to address a historic issue.

Papley will miss all pre-season matches and the club's opening rounds against Geelong, Essendon and GWS.

stories.headline: Origin star Young locked in for switch to PNG Chiefs
stories.summary: The PNG Chiefs have confirmed the signing of Hudson Young, with the NSW Origin star to leave Canberra at the end of the 2027 season.
stories.body:
NSW Origin back-rower Hudson Young has ended months of speculation, signing with the PNG Chiefs for their inaugural season.

The 28-year-old Canberra star has inked a deal to become the Chiefs' ninth official signing, the NRL's 19th team confirmed on Monday.

Young will honour the final year of his contract with the Raiders, where he has scored 59 tries across 155 NRL matches, before linking up with the Chiefs in 2028.

The second-rower's acquisition will bolster the Chiefs' forward pack.

"Hudson is a player that every club would like to have," Chiefs general manager of football Michael Chammas said on Monday.

"He is tough, competitive, incredibly consistent and brings an edge that lifts those around him."

Young played every minute of the NSW Blues' 2-1 Origin series win over Queensland this year, scoring two tries and making 115 tackles.

He has tallied six Test caps for Australia, but missed the Kangaroos' victorious 2026 World Cup campaign after rupturing his Achilles tendon in July.

Chiefs coach Willie Peters spent time with Young while working with the Australian Test side in 2025.

"Hudson plays with an aggressive style which I have no doubt the people of Papua New Guinea will love to see," Peters said.

"He will be an important leader in our group, and I look forward to working with him in season 2028 and beyond."

PNG have already signed Joey Manu, Brian To'o, Jarome Luai, Alex Johnston, Zac Lomax, Zac Laybutt, Matty Lees and Connor Watson.

AJ Brimson is poised to be the next cab off the rank, with Gold Coast agreeing to terms with PNG to make him the Chiefs' inaugural fullback.

The former Origin flyer was reportedly spotted playing golf with PNG Prime Minister James Marape while in the country to decide whether to consent to the move.

Former Dolphins No.7 Sean O'Sullivan is also set to join the club after next year's English Super League season.

The Chiefs have also met with Sydney Roosters halfback Sam Walker, and held preliminary talks with Brisbane pair Xavier Willison and Deine Mariner over a potential move.
